datasets.name: amazon-reviews
datasets.title: Amazon Reviews
datasets.description: The `amazon-reviews` network is a hypergraph where hyperedges are sets of product reviews on Amazon, as collected by Jianmo Ni, Jiacheng Li, and Julian McAuley (specifically, we use the collection of 5-core datasets). Nodes are labeled by their product categories.

datasets.name: citeseer-cocitation
datasets.title: CiteSeer Co-Citation
datasets.description: The CiteSeer co-citation network is a hypergraph where nodes are scientific papers from the CiteSeer dataset and hyperedges are sets of papers that are co-cited together by another paper. Each node is labeled with the paper's research field, chosen from six computer science topics: Agents, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Databases (DB), Information Retrieval (IR), Machine Learning (ML), and Human-Computer Interaction (HCI). This dataset is commonly used as a benchmark in hypergraph learning tasks.

datasets.name: coauth-DBLP
datasets.title: coauth-DBLP
datasets.description: This temporal higher-order network is a sequence of timestamped simplices, where each simplex is a set of nodes. In this dataset, nodes are authors and a simplex is a publication recorded on DBLP. Timestamps are the year of publication. > [!IMPORTANT] > In the original dataset, some nodes are repeated within hyperedges. This version of the dataset has removed these duplicates.

datasets.name: contact-high-school

datasets.name: cora-coauthorship
datasets.title: Cora Co-Authorship
datasets.description: The Cora co-authorship network is a hypergraph where nodes are authors from the Cora dataset and hyperedges are papers, representing sets of authors who collaborated on a publication. Each author is labeled with their primary research area, inferred from the majority research area of their publications. The research areas include Case-Based Reasoning, Genetic Algorithms, Neural Networks, Probabilistic Methods, Reinforcement Learning, Rule Learning, and Theory. This dataset is commonly used as a benchmark in hypergraph learning tasks for author classification and link prediction.

changelog: Dropped papers with only one author.

datasets.title: Cora Co-Citation

Each node is labeled with the paper's research field, chosen from seven computer science topics. This dataset is commonly used as a benchmark in hypergraph learning tasks.

datasets.name: dblp-coauthorship
datasets.title: DBLP Co-Authorship
datasets.description: The DBLP co-authorship network is a hypergraph where nodes are authors from the DBLP computer science bibliography database and hyperedges are papers, representing sets of authors who collaborated on a publication. Each author is labeled with their primary research area, inferred from the majority research area of their publications. datasets.name: drug-target-interaction
datasets.title: Drug-Target Interaction
datasets.description: The `drug-target-interaction` dataset is a combinatorial complex representing drug-target interactions and similarity relationships. The dataset is based on the work by Perlman et al., which combines multiple drug and gene similarity measures to predict drug-target interactions.

datasets.name: email-enron
datasets.title: Email Enron
datasets.description: This temporal higher-order network represents email communication in the Enron corpus. Nodes are email addresses, and each hyperedge contains the sender together with all recipients of an email message. > [!IMPORTANT] > Singleton hyperedges, such as emails sent only to oneself, are omitted in this dataset.

datasets.name: email-eu
datasets.title: Email EU
datasets.description: This temporal higher-order network represents email communication at a European research institution. Nodes are email addresses, and each hyperedge contains the sender together with all recipients of an email sharing the same timestamp. > [!IMPORTANT] > Singleton hyperedges, such as emails sent only to oneself, are omitted in this dataset.

datasets.name: florentine-families
datasets.title: Florentine Families
datasets.description: The Florentine families network represents marriage ties among prominent families in Renaissance Florence. We lifted the graph to its clique complex using `toponetx.graph_to_clique_complex`, so cliques become higher-dimensional simplices. This dataset is suited to test graph-based methods on a small historical social network and to exercise AHORN's clique-complex dataset structure.

datasets.name: MAG-10
datasets.title: MAG-10
datasets.description: The MAG-10 network is a subset of the Microsoft Academic Graph where nodes are authors, hyperedges correspond to a publication from those authors, and the hyperedges are categorized by one of 10 computer science conferences. If the same set of authors published at more than one conference, we used the most common venue as the category and any cases where there is a tie were discarded. Papers with more than 25 authors were omitted. > [!IMPORTANT] > Node `40706` has an erroneous label assignment in the source dataset. We assigned it to the first category.

datasets.name: MANTRA-2-manifolds
datasets.title: MANTRA 2-Manifolds
datasets.description: > [!NOTE] > The original MANTRA dataset includes both 2-manifolds and 3-manifolds. AHORN lists them as two separate datasets, with this page focusing on the 2-manifolds. You can find the 3-manifolds dataset here. The MANTRA collection provides simplicial complexes built from triangulations of closed 2- and 3-manifolds. Each manifold is represented by its vertex set and list of simplices (triangles or tetrahedra), enabling topological and combinatorial experiments across two dimensions. This dataset is derived from version 0.0.16 of MANTRA.

datasets.name: NDC-classes
datasets.title: NDC Classes
datasets.description: This temporal higher-order network is a sequence of timestamped simplices, where each simplex is a set of nodes. Under the Drug Listing Act of 1972, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration releases information on all commercial drugs going through the regulation of the agency, forming the National Drug Code (NDC) Directory. In this dataset, each simplex corresponds to a drug and the nodes are class labels applied to the drugs. Timestamps are in days and represent when the drug was first marketed.

datasets.name: NDC-substances
datasets.title: NDC Substances
datasets.description: This temporal higher-order network is a sequence of timestamped simplices, where each simplex is a set of nodes. Under the Drug Listing Act of 1972, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration releases information on all commercial drugs going through the regulation of the agency, forming the National Drug Code (NDC) Directory. In this dataset, each simplex corresponds to an NDC code for a drug, and the nodes are substances that make up the drug. Timestamps are in days and represent when the drug was first marketed.

datasets.name: walmart-trips
datasets.title: Walmart Trips
datasets.description: The walmart-trips network is a hypergraph where hyperedges are sets of co-purchased products at Walmart, as released as part of a Kaggle competition. Products are assigned to one of ten broad departments in which the product appears on walmart.com (e.g., "Clothing, Shoes, and Accessories"). Products not assigned to any of these departments are grouped into an "Other" category.
